title: Token-level perturbation log: int4 (AWQ/GPTQ) vs int8 onboarding contrast
content:
TL;DR:
We ran token-level perturbation logging across three quantization configs (int8 baseline, AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4) on our onboarding promptset (1.2k prompts split into curiosity/ops/formatting cohorts). Overall end-task deltas are small for many prompts but there are concentrated token-level log-prob shifts that correlate with specific cohorts (table-of-contents below). This doc records the raw per-token shifts, representative failure cases, quick hypotheses for causes (kv-cache alignment, softmax tail amplification, quant noise around small logits), and immediate mitigations to try before wider rollout.

Background / purpose:
- Context: onboarding a new Llama-style 30B variant into hosted catalog. Primary question: is AWQ-int4 or GPTQ-int4 acceptable relative to int8 for our production prompts?
- Why token-level logs: aggregate metrics (EM/ROUGE/QA-F1) mask brittle per-token probability shifts that lead to hallucination or truncation failures in conversation flows. We capture per-token logp changes (delta_logp = quant_logp - fp16_logp) and token sampling differences.

Dataset and prompt cohorts:
- Promptset size: 1,200 prompts (collected from customer templates + synthetic perturbations).
- Cohorts:
  - curiosity (open-ended, long-form creative) — 310 prompts
  - ops (instructional, config/CLI-style) — 420 prompts
  - formatting (tabular/markdown/CSV rounding) — 270 prompts
  - edge-short (very short single-turn prompts) — 200 prompts
- Seeded temperature: 0.0 for deterministic decoding (argmax) and 0.8 for sampling checks.

Experimental setup / runtime:
- Baseline: fp16 int8 hybrid (our current catalog baseline) run on A100, standard kernel set.
- Variants: AWQ-int4 (per-layer activation-aware quant) and GPTQ-int4 (per-channel weight-aware quant) exported with same vocab and tie-weights.
- Measurements captured per request: token index, token text, fp16_logp, quant_logp, delta_logp, chosen_token_fp16, chosen_token_quant, kv_cache_key_fingerprint, request_latency_ms.
- Run dates: 2025-02-20 to 2025-02-26. Randomized model order to avoid temporal drift.

Metrics collected (primary):
- prompt-em (instruction EM where applicable)
- average delta_logp per-token (mean and median)
- fraction of tokens with |delta_logp| > 0.5 nats (approx 0.72 bits)
- top-1 token disagreement rate (chosen_token_quant != chosen_token_fp16)
- truncated responses frequency (response shorter by >= 5 tokens)
- hallucination flag (heuristic matcher vs knowledge base for ops cohort)

High-level results summary:
- Aggregate end-task EM/QA-F1: int8 baseline -> 0.854 EM, AWQ-int4 -> 0.846 (-0.008), GPTQ-int4 -> 0.839 (-0.015).
- Mean delta_logp per-token: AWQ-int4 = -0.031 nats, GPTQ-int4 = -0.054 nats.
- Fraction tokens |delta| > 0.5: AWQ-int4 = 1.8%, GPTQ-int4 = 3.6% (int8 baseline ~0.6%).
- Top-1 disagreement rate (argmax): AWQ-int4 = 2.2%, GPTQ-int4 = 4.1%.
- Notable: formatting cohort shows higher disagreement on punctuation and table delimiters; ops cohort shows more hallucination cases for GPTQ-int4.

Token-level distribution notes (observed patterns):
- Long-tail amplification: For tokens with very low fp16_logp (< -6 nats), quantization sometimes increases logp (positive delta) causing some rare tokens to get over-represented during sampling. This is more common in GPTQ-int4 than AWQ.
- Boundary tokens: punctuation and newline tokens show concentrated negative delta in AWQ on the formatting cohort (likely due to activation clipping behavior in AWQ-algo).
- Softmax sharpness: GPTQ-int4 tends to make the top-1 probability sharper on some positions (top-1 probability increases, but second-best drops), meaning small logits perturbations affect sampling diversity.

Representative cases (selected from token-level logs) — anonymized and truncated:
1) Ops cohort (prompt id: ops-114):
   Prompt: "Given the following docker run command, explain the purpose of --rm and -it"
   fp16 output (first few tokens): "--rm removes the container after exit . -it allocates a tty and keeps stdin open ."
   GPTQ-int4 output (difference at tokens index 6-8): "--rm deletes the filesystem after exit . -it ..."
   token deltas (snippet):
     "removes" fp16_logp=-0.9, quant_logp=-1.7, delta=-0.8  (caused verb shift to 'deletes')
   Impact: small paraphrase but for ops customers this subtle verb change is undesirable (precision loss).

2) Formatting cohort (prompt id: fmt-071):
   Prompt: "Convert these rows to markdown table: ..."
   fp16 output punctuation sequence: "| Name | Age |" (correct column separators)
   AWQ-int4 produces a missing leading pipe in 12% of formatting prompts; token-level logs show newline token logp decreased by ~0.9 nats resulting in omission when beam width small.

3) Curiosity cohort (prompt id: cur-223):
   Long-form completion truncated 6 tokens earlier under GPTQ-int4 with cumulative negative delta on the last tokens (cumulative delta at truncation point = -3.6 nats). AWQ-int4 produced full-length but with slightly altered adjectives.

Per-cohort aggregated table (text form):
- curiosity: mean delta_logp AWQ=-0.028, GPTQ=-0.060; disagreement AWQ=1.9%, GPTQ=4.5%
- ops: mean delta_logp AWQ=-0.042, GPTQ=-0.083; disagreement AWQ=2.6%, GPTQ=5.2%
- formatting: mean delta_logp AWQ=-0.065, GPTQ=-0.034; disagreement AWQ=3.1%, GPTQ=2.0%
- edge-short: mean delta_logp AWQ=-0.018, GPTQ=-0.042; disagreement AWQ=1.4%, GPTQ=3.1%

Interpretation notes (quick):
- AWQ reduces large positive logp spikes (safer tail) but seems to penalize boundary/punctuation tokens (formatting cohort), likely due to activation clipping in layers processing token-level separators.
- GPTQ introduces more variance in low-prob tokens and increases top-1 disagreements in ops/curiosity, which maps to occasional hallucination or truncation.
- Int8 baseline still safest for ops use-cases where deterministic exact phrasing matters.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV-cache alignment: small differences in attention key/value accumulation produce token-level logp shifts that cascade in later positions (observed higher cumulative delta before truncation).
2) Quantization scale mismatch at embedding layer for punctuation tokens leads to systematic negative bias for those tokens in AWQ.
3) GPTQ per-channel rounding causes rare token logits to cross sampling thresholds, amplifying tail sampling behavior.

Immediate mitigations to evaluate (short-run):
- Per-cohort routing: route formatting prompts to int8 by rule until we patch AWQ behavior (fast fix in router policy).
- Calibration layer: add a tiny learned bias vector after final logits (per-token correction) trained on promptset deltas (cheap and small).
- Sampling safety: increase softmax temperature headroom and add nucleus/top-k constraints for GPTQ runs to reduce tail amplification.
- KV-cache fingerprinting: log and compare fingerprints post-deploy to monitor drift; if mismatch crosses threshold, failover to int8.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Ethan Park: implement per-path routing rule for formatting cohort -> int8 (eta: 48h).
- Ravi Menon: prototype a tiny post-logit calibration bias and test on 200 prompts across cohorts (eta: 1 week).
- Asha Nambiar: add regression unit to nightly job that computes fraction |delta|>0.5 and alerts above 2.5% for any cohort (eta: 72h).
- Maya Solis (me): run follow-up AWQ build with adjusted activation clipping thresholds and re-run subset (eta: 2 weeks).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is the punctuation bias constant across model sizes (we tried 7B quick check, saw similar but smaller effect)? Need systematic size sweep (7B, 13B, 30B).
- Can we craft a micro-finetune on promptset diff traces to correct token-level shifts cheaply? How does that interact with privacy constraints for customer prompts?
- For GPTQ tail amplification: would soft rounding or stochastic rounding during quantization reduce a lot of the outliers?

Appendix A: example token log snippet (format: index | token | fp16_logp | awq_logp | gptq_logp | delta_awq | delta_gptq)
0 | "|" | -0.12 | -0.90 | -0.25 | -0.78 | -0.13
1 | " Name" | -0.05 | -0.06 | -0.03 | -0.01 | +0.02
2 | " |" | -0.07 | -0.82 | -0.10 | -0.75 | -0.03

Appendix B: quick reproducibility notes:
- Repro command: workflows/runs/quant-eval/run_token_log.sh --model=<path> --prompts=onboard_v2.json --seed=42 --capture_logp true --outdir=gs://redwood-quant-logs/2025-02-token-pert
- Logs/artefacts: gs://redwood-quant-logs/2025-02-token-pert/ (raw logs, aggregated csvs, per-prompt diffs) [internal-only].

Appendix C: suggested experiments (next 2 weeks):
- Warm-start KV cache alignment experiment: run streaming generation where we inject fp16 prefix and then quantized suffix to identify breakpoints.
- Per-token calibration training: small convex probe on logits from quantized model to minimize KL on held-out promptset (evaluate generalization).
- Mixed-precision policy: keep embedding + final linear in int8, rest int4 variants — test cost vs fidelity tradeoffs.

Notes to reviewers: this doc contains anonymized prompt ids and redacted customer content where applicable. If we decide routing-by-cohort, coordinate with product to update public model capability notes.

End of token-level perturbation log.
